nodes.name: Player ground movement
nodes.purpose: Ground locomotion: input-to-speed curves, two-stage crouch stances, gravity and landing recovery, and the swept volume tests that keep the player capsule out of world geometry

nodes.name: First-person view
nodes.purpose: Look input response, the automatic pitch recentring that follows floor geometry ahead of the player, and the eye-height write that positions the first-person camera

nodes.name: Weapon handling
nodes.purpose: Per-hand weapon state: automatic fire rate accumulation, burst windows, the recoil animation that displaces the held weapon, and the ammunition each fire function demands

nodes.name: Damage resolution
nodes.purpose: Shield absorption before health, hit-zone and distance multipliers, and the flinch, knockback or death reaction applied when a character is hit

nodes.name: Enemy perception
nodes.purpose: Cone-limited sight with a distance-scaled detection roll, plus gunfire noise radii that reach nearby characters by radius over distance

nodes.name: World interaction
nodes.purpose: Choosing and triggering the nearest interactable object or door in front of the player, including per-model reach, activation angles, automatic doors and lift doors

cards.name: Ground speed targets
cards.summary: Turning control-pad and stick input into the forward and sideways speed fractions that the walk integrator consumes.
cards.behavior: Sideways movement has two sources. Digital left or right steps the sideways speed toward minus one or plus one in 0.2 increments per update, and an analogue strafe axis is scaled by 0.014285714365542 so a fully deflected stick reaches 1.0. Forward movement works the same way with a larger acceleration of one unit per update and the same analogue scale. Both axes are hard clamped to the range -1 to 1 before use, and the forward value is then multiplied by 1.08 plus any speed boost, so a fully deflected stick slightly exceeds the nominal walk speed. Whenever there is no forward input, or the stance is not standing, the counter that accumulates sustained forward running, and that later unlocks a speed boost, is reset to zero.

constants.name: digital strafe speed target
constants.unit: fraction of nominal walk speed, targeted per 60 Hz update

constants.name: strafe acceleration
constants.unit: walk-speed fraction per 60 Hz update

constants.name: stick deflection to speed scale
constants.unit: walk-speed fraction per stick unit, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: forward acceleration
constants.unit: walk-speed fraction per 60 Hz update

constants.name: full-deflection forward boost
constants.unit: multiplier on the clamped forward fraction, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: speed fraction clamp
constants.unit: walk-speed fraction limit on both axes, enforced per 60 Hz update

capabilities: digital and analogue ground speed targets
acceleration-limited speed changes with separate axes
clamped speed fractions with a small full-deflection boost

cards.name: Crouch stances
cards.summary: Two crouch heights, the interpolated body offset, and the speed and turn penalties each stance imposes.
cards.behavior: The stance machine has two crouch levels. Ducking lowers the view offset to minus 45 units and squatting lowers it to minus 90. The offset is eased toward the target with 0.5 acceleration and deceleration and a maximum of 5 units per update, and after each step the body is tested for headroom; if raising it would collide with a ceiling the previous offset, eye offset and speed are restored and the stance index steps back toward standing. Ducking halves forward and sideways speed and keeps 0.75 of the turn rate, while squatting multiplies speed by 0.35 and turn rate by 0.5. The same offset also yields a weapon position fraction of offset divided by minus 90, so the held weapon shifts as the body sinks.

constants.name: duck view offset
constants.unit: view units below standing eye height, targeted per 60 Hz update

constants.name: squat view offset
constants.unit: view units below standing eye height, targeted per 60 Hz update

constants.name: crouch offset acceleration
constants.unit: view units per 60 Hz update squared

constants.name: crouch offset maximum speed
constants.unit: view units per 60 Hz update

constants.name: duck speed scale
constants.unit: multiplier on forward and sideways speed, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: squat speed scale
constants.unit: multiplier on forward and sideways speed, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: squat turn scale
constants.unit: multiplier on turn speed, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: duck turn scale
constants.unit: multiplier on turn speed, applied per 60 Hz update

capabilities: two-stage crouch with eased body offset
ceiling-blocked crouch recovery
stance-specific speed and turn penalties

cards.name: Falling and landing recovery
cards.summary: Gravity integration while the feet are off the ground, the fall timer that kills, and the crouched recovery a hard landing imposes.
cards.behavior: While the feet sit above the ground height, vertical speed loses 0.277777777 units every update, which at the 60 Hz logic rate is close to 1000 units per second squared, and the vertical position is integrated with the average of the old and new speed. A fall that lasts longer than 240 ticks, or a drop below minus 30000 units, kills the player. On contact, a landing faster than minus 5 units per update bends the body down proportionally and a landing faster than minus 13.333333 units per update forces a full minus 90 crouch for 60 ticks, so heavier impacts take longer to stand up from. Landings faster than minus 6 units per update also emit footstep sounds, and a debug turbo mode multiplies the gravity step by five.

constants.name: gravity per update
constants.unit: vertical units per 60 Hz update squared (about 1000 units per second squared)

constants.name: fall death timer
constants.unit: ticks at 60 Hz (four seconds of uninterrupted falling)

constants.name: out-of-bounds floor
constants.unit: vertical world units, checked each 60 Hz update

constants.name: hard landing threshold
constants.unit: vertical units per 60 Hz update at contact

constants.name: soft landing threshold
constants.unit: vertical units per 60 Hz update at contact

constants.name: landing crouch hold
constants.unit: ticks at 60 Hz before the crouch begins to release

constants.name: landing footstep threshold
constants.unit: vertical units per 60 Hz update at contact

capabilities: per-update gravity integration with averaged position step

cards.name: Collision sweep and step-up
cards.summary: Testing a movement delta against world geometry with the player capsule, and stepping small heights instead of blocking on them.
cards.behavior: A movement delta whose horizontal components are all shorter than half the capsule radius runs a single volume overlap test at the destination, while a longer delta also runs a cylinder move test from the old position so fast movement cannot tunnel through thin geometry. Room lists come from an exhaustive portal trace that records up to 20 rooms, and the capsule vertical extent is passed explicitly so floors, ceilings and steps all take part in the same test. A vertical move test lowers the capsule bottom by 0.1 units before overlapping geometry so a body resting exactly on a surface is still detected, and ladder probing uses 1.2 times the capsule radius to find a climbable surface.

constants.name: sweep threshold
constants.unit: fraction of capsule radius per 60 Hz update above which a cylinder move test is added

constants.name: vertical test margin
constants.unit: world units subtracted from the capsule bottom per vertical test at 60 Hz

constants.name: ladder probe radius
constants.unit: capsule radius multiplier, tested each 60 Hz update

constants.name: room trace limit
constants.unit: rooms recorded per collision sweep at 60 Hz

capabilities: short-step volume test versus full cylinder sweep
vertical extent included in every horizontal test
ceiling and step tolerance margins

cards.name: Analogue look response
cards.summary: Stick look is normalised, squared for finer small inputs, accelerated into a turn rate and clamped to a full vertical sweep.
cards.behavior: Vertical and horizontal deflection is divided by 70 and clamped to the range -1 to 1. The normalised value keeps its sign but is multiplied by itself, so small deflections turn very slowly while full deflection turns at the maximum. The resulting look speed is scaled by the current vertical field of view divided by 60, so a narrowed view changes sensitivity. Look speed grows by 0.05 per update while input pushes the same way and only by 0.0125 when input reverses it, clamped to a limit of 0.7 times the field-of-view scale, and pitch is integrated at 3.5 times the look speed. Vertical angle is wrapped into a single turn and clamped to plus or minus 90 degrees so the view cannot pass the vertical.

constants.name: stick normalisation
constants.unit: stick units for full look deflection, sampled per 60 Hz update

constants.name: look speed acceleration
constants.unit: look speed units per 60 Hz update

constants.name: look speed decay
constants.unit: look speed units per 60 Hz update

constants.name: field-of-view sensitivity divisor
constants.unit: degrees of vertical field of view per look speed unit, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: look speed limit scale
constants.unit: multiplier on field-of-view scaled look speed limit, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: pitch integration gain
constants.unit: degrees of pitch per look speed unit per 60 Hz update

constants.name: pitch clamp
constants.unit: degrees above and below the horizon, enforced each 60 Hz update

capabilities: sign-preserving squared stick response

cards.name: Pitch recentring over the floor
cards.summary: When the player runs forward without touching the vertical look axis, the view drifts back to a pitch that follows the floor ahead.
cards.behavior: A lookahead pitch is built by tracing up to 400 units along the view direction and probing the floor at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 percent of the unobstructed distance. Samples whose floor height is within about 200 units of the current ground are converted to angles, clamped to the band from minus 50 to plus 40 degrees, and the surviving samples are thinned until one median remains. A positive result is damped by 0.86666667461395, and a trace that hits nothing leaves the default pitch of minus 4 degrees. Recentring only engages when forward deflection exceeds 60 stick units and the view is more than 5 degrees above or 10 degrees below the target, and it moves to the target using the same acceleration and decay as manual look before stopping exactly on it.

constants.name: lookahead default pitch
constants.unit: degrees below the horizon when no floor sample applies, per 60 Hz update

constants.name: lookahead trace length
constants.unit: world units along the view direction per 60 Hz update

constants.name: lookahead sample spacing
constants.unit: fraction of the traced distance per probe, one probe set per 60 Hz update

constants.name: lookahead downward limit
constants.unit: degrees below the horizon accepted per 60 Hz update

constants.name: lookahead upward limit
constants.unit: degrees above the horizon accepted per 60 Hz update

constants.name: upward lookahead damping
constants.unit: multiplier on positive lookahead pitch per 60 Hz update

constants.name: recentre upward dead zone
constants.unit: degrees above the lookahead target, sampled per 60 Hz update

constants.name: recentre downward dead zone
constants.unit: degrees below the lookahead target, sampled per 60 Hz update

constants.name: recentre forward deflection threshold
constants.unit: stick units of forward deflection, sampled per 60 Hz update

capabilities: floor-following lookahead pitch sampling

cards.name: Automatic fire rate
cards.summary: Automatic weapons turn a rounds-per-minute figure into whole shots per update, carrying the fractional remainder between updates.
cards.behavior: An automatic fire function derives shots per update from its current rate: the interpolated rounds per minute is divided by 60 for rounds per second and again by 60 for rounds per 60 Hz update, then multiplied by the number of updates this frame and added to a per-hand remainder. The whole part is taken as the shots to fire now and the fraction is stored for next time, so the average rate stays exact even at rates that are not a whole number of shots per update. If the accumulator owes nothing, an idle hand still fires one shot while a hand already busy with the previous shot stops firing, and one-shot functions simply request a single shot per trigger update. Each shot also stamps the next allowed shot frame from the fire-slot duration so sound and rate cannot double up.

constants.name: rounds-per-minute divisor
constants.unit: rounds per minute per shot per second of a 60 Hz update

constants.name: single-shot count
constants.unit: shots per 60 Hz update for non-automatic fire functions

capabilities: fractional shot accumulation across updates
rate interpolation from barrel spin fraction
fire-slot frame gating for repeats and sound

cards.name: Secondary fire requirements
cards.summary: Every weapon carries two fire functions, and each function can demand a different minimum amount of loaded ammunition before it may fire.
cards.behavior: The weapon state holds two function slots and the active slot flips between them through a change-function state that plays the transition animation for that direction and then returns to idle. Before a function is allowed to fire its minimum clip quantity is checked: one round by default, two shells for a double-charge alternate function, and four darts for the alternate function of a dart launcher, which are also the amounts deducted by a single use. When the active function cannot be satisfied the hand switches slots, starts a reload, or reports depletion so the idle state can choose an alternate weapon or function instead.

constants.name: default minimum clip
constants.unit: rounds required per 60 Hz update before a function may fire

constants.name: double-charge alternate minimum
constants.unit: shells required per 60 Hz update before the alternate function may fire

constants.name: dart alternate minimum
constants.unit: darts required per 60 Hz update before the alternate function may fire

constants.name: alternate function slot
constants.unit: function index (zero primary, one alternate), sampled per 60 Hz update

capabilities: two fire functions per weapon with animated switching
function-specific minimum clip quantities
automatic slot change or reload when a function cannot fire

cards.name: Weapon recoil animation
cards.summary: A per-weapon recoil timeline that rotates and slides the held weapon away from the aim point and then blends it back.
cards.behavior: While a shot recoil window is open, a rise phase drives the weapon rotation and translation with a quarter-sine and a fall phase blends back with a half-cosine plus a half offset. Translation is a fraction of the weapon offset from the aim point, scaled by the weapon recoil distance divided by 1000, and the rotation ends at a full turn minus the recoil angle. A trigger release followed by a press inside the refire window restarts the cycle from the current rotation and position, so rapid taps keep the weapon kicked up instead of letting it settle. The recoil releases at the end of the recoil window when a re-fire was queued, or only after the weapon recovery time has also elapsed.

constants.name: recoil translation divisor
constants.unit: world units per recoil distance unit, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: rise phase quarter turn
constants.unit: degrees of sine phase per recoil frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: fall phase half turn
constants.unit: degrees of cosine phase per recoil frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: blend midpoint
constants.unit: fraction that centres the cosine fall curve, applied per 60 Hz update

capabilities: sine rise and cosine settle recoil curves
recoil restarted from the current offset on rapid re-fire
per-weapon recoil distance and angle

cards.name: Shield absorption
cards.summary: Shields soak damage before health, divide incoming damage by an armour scale, and discard the remainder when they break.
cards.behavior: A character carrying shield points absorbs damage before health is touched. The incoming amount is divided by an armour scale, which is 1 for ordinary characters and 4 for a defensive bot personality, and when the shield covers that quotient the shield drops by it and the shot does no health damage at all. When the shield cannot cover the quotient it is set to zero and the leftover damage is discarded rather than carried into health, while a shield-hit effect plays at the impact point. A wall-piercing scoped shot forces shield damage and multiplies the damage by 10, and the one-hit-kill multiplayer option empties the shield and zeroes the damage. Each shield point is worth an eighth of the armour bar shown to the player.

constants.name: shield points per armour bar
constants.unit: armour bar fraction per shield point, updated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: defensive armour scale
constants.unit: damage divisor applied to shielded hits, once per 60 Hz update

constants.name: wall-piercing damage scale
constants.unit: damage multiplier for the wall-piercing scoped shot, applied once per 60 Hz update

capabilities: shield-first damage order
armour scale division against shields
leftover damage discarded when a shield breaks

cards.name: Hit zone damage
cards.summary: Damage multipliers by body part, added distance falloff for multi-pellet weapons, and difficulty scaling for player shots.
cards.behavior: Once shields have been resolved, damage passes through a set of body-part multipliers. General-area hits are halved and then treated as torso hits, and general-half hits are quartered for the same reason. Head hits multiply damage by 4 and additionally by 25 when the attacker is the player and no shield absorbed the shot, which is what makes a clean headshot lethal. Torso hits double damage, and hits to a held gun or a hat do nothing. Multi-pellet weapons scale their damage by distance from the shooter: a random 4 to 6 times inside 200 units, 3 to 4 times inside 400, 2 to 3 times inside 800 and 1 to 2 times inside 1600.

constants.name: general hit scale
constants.unit: damage multiplier before torso handling, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: general-half hit scale
constants.unit: damage multiplier before torso handling, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: head hit multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier per 60 Hz update

constants.name: player headshot scale
constants.unit: additional damage multiplier when the player shoots a head, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: closest pellet band
constants.unit: world units from the shooter, evaluated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: middle pellet band
constants.unit: world units from the shooter, evaluated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: farthest pellet band
constants.unit: world units from the shooter, evaluated per 60 Hz update

capabilities: body-part damage multipliers

cards.name: Damage reaction
cards.summary: What a hit does to a target that survives it: an impact-force driven flinch, a forced slide for mechanical bodies, and death once damage reaches the maximum.
cards.behavior: Every hit adds to the target's accumulated damage, and once that total reaches the character's maximum damage the death sequence starts instead of a flinch. Mechanical and vehicle-like bodies convert the weapon impact force into a short forced slide whose duration is the strength times 15, defaulting to 6 when the weapon reports no impact force and halving the strength for the heaviest chassis. Small drone targets are pushed with four times their impact strength instead. Everyone else plays a directional flinch animation chosen by the hit angle and hit part, while a target that is already knocked out skips the flinch entirely.

constants.name: default impact strength
constants.unit: impact force units when a weapon reports none, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: drone push scale
constants.unit: impact force multiplier on drone bodies, applied per hit at 60 Hz

constants.name: heavy chassis strength scale
constants.unit: impact force multiplier on the heaviest chassis, applied per hit at 60 Hz

constants.name: impact slide duration scale
constants.unit: forced-slide ticks at 60 Hz per impact strength unit

capabilities: accumulated damage compared against a per-character maximum
impact-force driven forced slide for mechanical bodies
angle-selected flinch animations for living targets

cards.name: Guard sight cone
cards.summary: A character sees a target only inside a wide but finite cone, within a range scaled by a vision statistic, after a distance-scaled random roll and a line-of-sight trace.
cards.behavior: The bearing to the target is compared with the character's facing and must fall below 110 degrees or above 250 degrees around the circle, which leaves a blind sector directly behind. Range is the vision statistic squared times 10000, with an unconditional near-field allowance of 40000 squared units, and the candidate must also be inside the fog distance. Within the cone the detection divisor starts at distance times 0.001875 and is multiplied upward as the target moves outside the central 45 degrees, and detection succeeds only when a random roll modulo that divisor is zero, so distant or peripheral targets are noticed on fewer updates. A successful roll must still pass a line-of-sight trace, and the defaults give a new character a vision statistic of 250 and a hearing scale of 1.

constants.unit: degrees either side of facing, tested per 60 Hz update

constants.name: blind sector start angle

constants.name: vision range square scale

constants.name: near-field squared range

constants.name: detection divisor scale

constants.name: central peripheral cone
constants.unit: degrees either side of facing before the divisor is widened, tested per 60 Hz update

constants.name: peripheral widening scale

cards.name: Gunfire noise and hearing
cards.summary: Firing builds a noise radius per hand that decays over time, and nearby characters convert that radius into a distance-based detection score.
cards.behavior: Each firing hand accumulates a noise radius up to a per-weapon maximum and decays back toward a minimum, with the decay amount taken from either a base speed or a remaining-radius speed divided by a 60 frame timebase, whichever is larger. The larger radius of the two hands is passed to a world query that visits every character already targeting the player and computes the radius times 100 times that character's hearing scale times 1.075, divided by the distance to the player, substituting 2 when the two positions coincide. A score above 1 records a hearing event for that character, and a remembered event stays valid for 600 ticks before it expires.

constants.name: hearing margin
constants.unit: fraction added to the hearing multiplier per 60 Hz update

constants.name: noise radius to hearing scale
constants.unit: hearing units per noise radius unit per 60 Hz update

constants.name: zero-distance fallback
constants.unit: world units substituted when attacker and listener coincide, per 60 Hz update

constants.name: hearing score threshold
constants.unit: hearing score needed to record a sound, checked per 60 Hz update

constants.name: noise decay timebase
constants.unit: frames per second of the decay timebase, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: hearing memory
constants.unit: ticks at 60 Hz (ten seconds) before a remembered sound expires

capabilities: per-hand noise radius with rise and decay

cards.name: Object interaction reach
cards.summary: Choosing the interaction target from the on-screen prop list using per-model reach, a narrow bearing window and a line-of-sight check.
cards.behavior: Interaction walks the on-screen prop list from nearest to farthest and stops at the first candidate that passes its test. An object qualifies when it is flagged interactable or is an alarm, terminal, lift, grab target or mountable vehicle, and grab targets and vehicles additionally require a standing stance with zero crouch offset. Reach defaults to 200 units, drops to 100 for objects flagged as short range and rises to 280, 300 or 500 for capsule-shaped, car-sized and shuttle-sized models. The target must also sit within 22.5 degrees of the view bearing in the horizontal plane and pass a line-of-sight trace unless it opts out. The chosen prop is then routed to the object or door handler and its tick operation.

constants.unit: world units, tested per 60 Hz update

cards.name: Door handling
cards.summary: Doors open through proximity plus a face-on angle test, toggle direction from how far open they already are, and can open automatically.
cards.behavior: A door becomes a candidate when the player is within 200 units horizontally and 200 units vertically of the door start position, or within 150 units of the door pad volume or bounding box while sharing a room. The activation angles must lie within 20 degrees of the player's view, and a door that only slides sideways is considered only when the player is within 30 units of its pad volume. Activating a door in the idle state closes it when it is already more than half open and opens it otherwise, while opening or waiting doors close and closing doors open, and lift doors forward the request to their lift first. Automatic doors compare which side of the door the player stands on with the player's own facing and open when the player is approaching the door from behind it, so the door swings away rather than into them.

constants.unit: world units horizontally and vertically, tested per 60 Hz update
